Processor mask helpers, online and possible iteration, current processor identity, and idle wake predicate.
Bringup helpers for nonboot processors, idle fork, hotplug thread init, processor count setters, bit search, and post bringup done handling.
Workqueue, completion, hypervisor pinning, and scheduler primitives used by on cpu calls and hotplug threads.
Soft interrupt vector count, action structure, numeric vector identities, scheduler bit value, and bottom half offset values.
Daemon wake predicate, daemon task lifecycle, forced threading test, own stack dispatch, statistics, tracing, RCU quiescent handling, reschedule test, and accounting helpers.
Preempt count layout, migration control, RCU read section rules, per processor local lock, debug and trace configuration behavior.

findings.text: Provides a boolean query that reports whether the call data lock stuck counter is nonzero, without changing any state.
Single call interprocessor interrupt entry that drains the local single call queue when that interrupt arrives.

Process context drain of the local single call queue that returns at once when the queue looks empty, otherwise preserves interrupt state, snapshots pending soft interrupt state, drains the queue, runs post flush soft interrupt handling when new pending state appeared, then restores interrupts.

Attempts nonblocking dispatch of caller owned call data to one processor, reporting busy when the data already appears locked, otherwise marking it locked with ordering before handing it to the single execution helper, holding preemption disabled across check and hand off.
Dispatches a callback to any processor in a caller mask by delegating to the single target helper with an any selector.
Broadcasts a callback under a per processor condition and mask, always including local execution and adding synchronous wait behavior when requested, then delegating to the conditional many helper.
Synchronously interrupts all processors after a full memory barrier by broadcasting an empty callback and waiting for completion.
Walks all possible processors and wakes those that are online and idle and not local, disabling preemption separately around each processor check.
Non destructively reports whether any processor in a mask currently has a nonempty single call queue.

Synchronously runs a caller function on a chosen online processor using an on stack work item plus completion queued to the per processor system workqueue, rejecting out of range or offline targets, optionally recording a physical identity for hypervisor pinning, and returning the function result.

The on cpu work callback recovers its container from the work item, pins the virtual processor when a nonnegative selector was recorded, invokes the stored function with stored data, unpins afterwards, records the return value and signals completion.

Boot time secondary processor bringup initializes idle threads and hotplug threads, announces bringup, brings up nonboot processors limited by a setup maximum, reports online node and processor counts with plural handling, then performs post bringup cleanup.
Derives the active processor count from one plus the highest set bit in the possible mask, and enables an inlined mask optimization when preemption is configured and the mask fits in one word.

Early boot parameters control processor topology: one disables symmetric multiprocessing and clears the setup maximum, one clamps the processor identifier count when the value is positive and below current limit, one stores the setup maximum and disables support when zero; the architecture disable hook is a weak empty default.

Idle thread setup records the current task in the per processor idle slot for the boot processor, and creates an idle task for every other possible processor, logging a failure without aborting when creation fails.

Hotplug thread list management creates threads by walking registrations forward under mutex and stopping on first failure, unparks by walking forward, parks by walking backward and skipping self parking entries without a task, and unregisters by removing under reader plus mutex protection then destroying threads.

Process context soft interrupt entry that does nothing when already in interrupt context, otherwise preserves interrupt state, checks pending state once, dispatches on a dedicated stack when pending, then restores interrupts.
Interrupt stack soft interrupt entry that delegates to the common handler in direct mode rather than daemon mode.

Post flush helper compares pending soft interrupt state before and after a single call queue drain and invokes soft interrupt handling only when the state changed, warning when growth outside the scheduler bit is observed.

One soft interrupt invoke variant only wakes the per processor daemon when a wake predicate holds; the other variant runs the handler directly on the current or dedicated stack when threaded interrupts are not forced or no daemon task exists, otherwise wakes the daemon.

Bottom half disable and enable family maintains nested per task and per processor disable counts, with one configuration using counts plus RCU and migration or local lock control and another using preempt count adjustments plus lockdep and tracing hooks.

Interrupt entry path records raw entry, rearms deferred timers, conditionally enters tick handling for full dynticks or idle tasks in base hard interrupt level, and accounts hard interrupt entry; the outer wrapper adds context tracking entry, while exit logic propagates timer updates for core idle or full dynticks processors outside hard interrupt context.

Daemon and handler wrappers pair disable and enable around soft interrupt execution: one daemon variant brackets execution with bottom half disable plus interrupt disable and a matching release plus enable, the other only toggles interrupts; handler begin and end are either empty or a disable and enable pair with an interrupt context check.

Common soft interrupt handling snapshots pending state, marks handler begin with lockdep and accounting, clears pending before enabling interrupts, dispatches set vectors from low to high with statistics and tracing, then disables interrupts and rechecks pending, repeating while within a time budget without reschedule need and restart budget remaining, otherwise waking the daemon before balanced exit and flag restoration.

Soft interrupt handling temporarily clears the memory allocation flag from current task flags and restores only that flag on exit, and verifies that each vector handler preserves preemption nesting, logging and restoring on mismatch.

First entry into a bottom half disabled region acquires read tracking plus RCU and migration or local lock protection when preemptible, while last exit releases them; intermediate nesting only adjusts counters, and re enabling from preemptible context with pending work may run handlers directly instead of only waking the daemon.

Empty header definitions for idle setup and empty handler and lockdep variants describe configurations without symmetric multiprocessing or without tracing and lock validation, where those operations are no operations or report not in hard interrupt context.

A dedicated mutex serializes all walks of the hotplug thread registration list; creation and unpark traverse forward, parking traverses backward, and unregistration nests that mutex inside the processor set reader lock.

Bottom half control pairs a named per processor lockdep map acquire on disable with a release on enable or daemon exit, plus RCU read protection and either migration disable or a per processor local lock held from first disable to last enable.

Queue flush and soft interrupt dispatch preserve interrupt state with save and restore, enable interrupts only while invoking vector actions, disable before re sampling pending state, and assert disabled state inside low level enable and enabled state inside high level enable.

Async single dispatch and idle wake checks hold preemption disabled across the queue state test and hand off, and hotplug thread state checks hold preemption disabled across stop and park tests before sleeping or running.

On cpu call container holds a work item, a completion, a function returning an integer, an opaque data pointer, an integer result slot and an integer processor selector where negative means no pinning.

Hotplug thread private data holds a processor number, a status word and a pointer to its registration; status uses three ordered values meaning none then active then parked, and idle tasks are kept in a per processor pointer table.

Soft interrupt control state comprises a per processor vector table sized by the number of soft interrupts and aligned to avoid sharing, a per processor daemon task pointer, a per processor bottom half control with a local lock plus count, per processor hard interrupt enable and context integers, a per processor interrupt disable state word, a per processor nonmaskable nesting counter, and a named local bottom half lockdep map marked as per processor with free outer wait and config inner wait.
Interrupt save helpers expose a per processor saved state word plus a save entry that records flags and an enable entry that restores enabled state.

Each hotplug thread loops interruptibly: stop request exits after running cleanup when previously set up and freeing private data; park request runs park handling when active then parks and rechecks for stop; otherwise none runs setup then becomes active, parked runs unpark then becomes active, active either sleeps when its run predicate is false or runs its function when true, always verifying it runs on its assigned processor outside sleep.

Soft interrupt pending handling moves from snapshot to clear to enabled dispatch to disabled recheck, either looping for another round while budget remains or delegating remainder to the daemon, with tracing and accounting bracketing the whole sequence.

Lockdep soft interrupt tracking temporarily exits hard interrupt context when nested, enters soft interrupt context, then on exit leaves soft interrupt context and re enters hard interrupt context when it had been active, returning whether nesting was present; the alternate variant does nothing and reports no nesting.

Callable and boot entries in this lane include the single call interrupt handler, both soft interrupt dispatch entries, both interrupt entry wrappers, secondary processor bringup, three early parameter handlers, the on cpu work callback, and the hotplug thread main loop.

Mismatched preemption nesting across a vector handler, bottom half control invoked from hard interrupt context, pending growth beyond the scheduler bit after a queue drain, unbalanced or negative disable counts, unexpected per processor counts in nonpreemptible entry, interrupt state violations on handler exit, and running a hotplug thread on the wrong processor are all treated as warnings or fatal checks with restoration where possible.
Failure to allocate an idle task for a possible processor is logged as an error but does not abort initialization, leaving that per processor slot empty.
Synchronous call flag occupies bit zero and local execution flag occupies bit one of the call flags word.

Scheduler soft interrupt mask selects only the scheduler bit, the direct handling time budget corresponds to two milliseconds expressed in timer ticks, and the direct handling restart bound is ten iterations.
Hotplug thread lifecycle values are ordered with none as zero, active next, and parked last.
First half of the soft interrupt name table in vector order is high priority, timer, transmit networking, receive networking and block.
Second half of the soft interrupt name table in vector order is poll, tasklet, scheduler, high resolution timer and read copy update.
Both the setup processor maximum and the processor identifier count default to the build time processor limit, and a zero setup maximum selects no secondary processor support.
A false static key records whether the interprocessor mask fast path is inlined, enabled only for small masks.
Log prefix uses the module name and trace points are instantiated in this translation unit, with an include guard defining the boot header sentinel.
